messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT - Elevated 5xx from private VPC egress gateway (eu-west-1-private-gw-1). All downstream customer traffic to external model providers showing 502/503/504. Trigger: gateway-error-rate > 5% for 5m. Initial detection 2026-03-15T08:12:01Z
ben (oncall-sre): Acknowledging, I’m on it. Paging netops + infra. Putting page channel on-call.
ben (oncall-sre): Quick status: error rate peaked ~8.3% on the gateway, increased latency for private deployments, hosted unaffected. Customers: 3 Dedicated and 2 Private tenants impacted (billing eu-west).
carla (netops): I’m looking at the peering and SG rules now. Any recent changes?
dave (eng-infra): I saw a config apply to the private-gw ASG ~10m ago from user `infra-jenkins` — deploying security-group rollback. Pulling audit.
ben (oncall-sre): attach logs from gateway?
incident-bot: Attached logs: /var/log/gw/eu-west-1-private-gw-1/2026-03-15.log (tail below)
incident-bot: ```
Mar 15 08:09:50 gateway-1 proxy: upstream response code=502, host=model-provider-a.net, conn=pool-3
Mar 15 08:10:02 gateway-1 proxy: upstream response code=504, host=model-provider-b.net, conn=pool-7
Mar 15 08:10:50 gateway-1 netfilter: DROP src=10.2.45.0/24 dst=35.200.90.123 sport=49152-65535 dport=443 rule=sg-outbound-restrict
Mar 15 08:11:12 gateway-1 kernel: conntrack: table full? no, but high usage
```
carla (netops): That SG line looks suspicious: `sg-outbound-restrict` got applied at 08:08:55. I’m pulling the change record.
carla (netops): Change origin: `infra-jenkins` deploy job `private-egress-hardening` — rule reduced ephemeral port range to 49152-51200 (previously 49152-65535).
dave (eng-infra): Ok that would cause peer NAT exhaustion when multiple upstream connections open. Those 5xxs fit NAT port depletion or ephemeral whitelisting causing upstream resets.
ben (oncall-sre): Can we revert that SG quickly? Carla, can you roll back? If netops needs a safe mitigation we can fail traffic to standby NAT/gateway pair.
carla (netops): Rolling back now. Command: ```
aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d --protocol tcp --port 49152-51200 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0
# then re-authorize ephemeral full range
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d --protocol tcp --port 49152-65535 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0
```
carla (netops): Applied rollback at 08:13:40Z. Please monitor.
dave (eng-infra): Pushing a short-lived route to standby NAT to relieve pressure while we validate: ```
# create route in private subnet route table
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0f1e2d3c --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0b2c3d4e
```
dave (eng-infra): Route applied at 08:14:05Z.
ben (oncall-sre): Observability: error rate dropped to 3.1% at 08:15, latency normalizing. Still seeing spikes to model-provider-b.
ellie (customer-success): Heads up — I’ve DM’d affected customers with an interim note. One customer reported model inference failing for a small subset of requests. No PII impacted.
carla (netops): Confirmed: SG rollback removed restrictive outbound rule. NAT port usage metrics show ephemeral pool freed from 98% -> 32% usage in 2 min.
ben (oncall-sre): Good. Next steps: keep standby route for 20 mins, monitor for reoccurrence, start RCA. Carola, can you give root cause summary for initial incident? (cc: exec-sre)
carla (netops): Root cause (initial): automated infra job tightened outbound ephemeral ports in `sg-outbound-restrict` which unintentionally limited ephemeral port range used to NAT. Under normal fanout this caused source port exhaustion -> upstream connection resets -> gateway returned 502/504.
dave (eng-infra): Mitigation timeline: 08:08 change applied -> 08:12 alerts -> 08:13 SG rollback -> 08:14 standby route -> 08:15 error rates reduced.
ben (oncall-sre): Escalation: no customer billing impact expected, some request retries were served. Ellie, pass along that we’re investigating and will follow up with postmortem and timeline.
ellie (customer-success): Sending update to customers now with ETA for root cause and RCA.
ben (oncall-sre): Action items (short):
- carla: create revert guard in infra CI to block ephemeral-port-range changes without manual approval (assigned)
- dave: automate NAT port usage alert at 80% -> page (assigned)
- ben: write initial incident summary and coordinate postmortem (assigned)
- infra: add canary test for private egress to model providers during SG changes (assigned)
carla (netops): Added temporary CI hold at 08:22. Will open CL for manual approval step.
dave (eng-infra): Deploy-bot notes: rollback job executed: `infra-jenkins #452` -> status SUCCESS at 08:13. Deploy-bot: ```
[INFO] Reverted security-group sg-0a1b2c3d outbound rule. job=infra-jenkins/452
```
ben (oncall-sre): Are we comfortable closing this paging incident or keep monitoring?
carla (netops): Keep monitoring for 30m. I’ll leave a watch on conntrack and nat metrics.
ben (oncall-sre): Agreed. I’ll update the incident channel and create postmortem draft. Closing urgent pager at 08:23 but leaving the thread open for RCA and follow-ups.
ellie (customer-success): Customers updated. No escalations yet. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (high) at 08:23:14Z. Follow-up required: RCA and CI guard.
ben (oncall-sre): Final note: potential follow-up is to audit infra jobs that alter SGs for private egress. Will include list of recent runs in the postmortem.
carla (netops): I’ll attach the change diff to the RCA.
dave (eng-infra): I’ll schedule the NAT alert and canary test PRs.
ben (oncall-sre): Thanks all. Handoff to postmortem owners.
